GOAL: Orient before proposing the metric; find the Issue #126 artefacts (SID tables, behaviour reference, recall list) so the proposal is grounded in the real file/array shapes.
READ: searched the tool catalog for append_progress (found: tools.progress.append_progress); next step is a read-only listing of the working directory /fs04/ar57/wenyu/GeneRec/results/research/issue126/metric_round/agents/metric_ideation_1 and its parents.
OBSERVED: progress tool exists; workspace is a per-agent metric-ideation folder with no git repo.
EVIDENCE: tool catalog entry tools.progress.append_progress; env block (working directory).
REASONING: Before fixing a formula I need to know whether the frozen reference exposes per-item source/target vectors and what the exported SID table columns are, so INPUTS can be named precisely.
OPEN: what files exist locally, whether a Q_H implementation is readable, and whether item counts/pair counts match 24587/97.

GOAL: Fix the design-space slot before writing, using only the contract text (no filesystem access was available: read/glob/grep are permission-denied and no fs tool exists in this session's catalog).
READ: the task contract + the five "already known" measurements; I explicitly checked for file access (tools.* search for glob/grep/read/bash -> none usable; direct read -> permission.rejected).
OBSERVED: level-1 codebook is 256 codes over 24587 items (~96 items/cell, so cell size is near-uniform in every run). Bucket count is therefore almost constant across the 97 tables, which is exactly why bucket count/same-bucket ratio are flat (-0.065 / weak): the runs differ in WHICH items share a code, not in HOW MANY codes are used. Q_H succeeds at level 1 (+0.634) because it reads that "which", and fails at levels 2-3 (+0.287/+0.393) because there the prefix is nearly an item identifier.
REASONING: three consequences. (1) Any functional of the cell-size histogram is dead on arrival. (2) Any functional of the SID prefix tree alone (Poincare tree embedding, LCA depth, tree distance between items) is a MONOTONE function of the depth of the lowest common ancestor, i.e. a graded same-bucket ratio - excluded by the contract and weak by the known result. So the curvature must act on the frozen reference geometry, not on the code tree. (3) With unit-norm reference vectors a fixed-radius exp-map puts every item on a sphere and the Poincare distance collapses to a monotone function of cosine -> "Euclidean in disguise". Therefore the design needs a NON-CONSTANT radial coordinate; I use the training-split target frequency (allowed input) as the radius profile, which is also the right allocation story (fine discrimination near the origin where query mass is, exponential room for rare items).
OPEN: exact form of the one scalar over the level-1 cells; decided next.
